subject: URGENT: embeddings service regression after catalog rollout
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice@rapidretail.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Embedding queries — p99 spike since catalog update

Hi Marissa,

We're seeing a regression on the embeddings endpoint starting overnight (approx 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC) that coincides with your model catalog rollout. p95 latency is up ~2-3x and p99 has spiked from ~180ms to ~1.2s for our 512-d vector requests. This is impacting two production pipelines (search rerank and personalization) and causing timeouts on our ingestion workers.

I've attached a small slice of traces and the latency_report_0316.csv. Our engineering lead is copied. Can we get an urgent sync / remediation plan? We need an ETA — customers are seeing timeouts.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Chen
Head of Data Platform, RapidRetail
attachments: rapidretail_traces_0316.json, latency_report_0316.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: alice@rapidretail.com
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Embedding queries — p99 spike since catalog update

Folks — forwarding RapidRetail's report. They called this morning; escalation wanted. Initial asks: (1) quick triage, (2) temporary mitigation (rollback or routing to previous model variant), (3) communication & credits.

Connor: can you pull engine metrics (p95/p99 by model variant, kernel selection, and rack) for the last 48h? Hannah: if this looks like a runtime/quantization regression, we need an emergency rollback plan and a short executive note I can send to the customer.

I'll stand up a 15-min triage if useful.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Embedding queries — p99 spike since catalog update

I'm looking at the serving telemetry now. Quick notes:
- p95 jumped from ~210ms to ~520ms around 2026-03-15T02:10:00Z; p99 from ~180ms to ~1.2s.
- The spike maps to the catalog commit that changed the default embedding variant from "embed-small-v2" to "embed-small-v2-quant" for the catalog alias used by RapidRetail.
- We see a higher-than-expected CPU on model hosts using older CUDA kernels where the quantized path triggers slower fallback kernels. KV cache hit rates also dropped for that variant.

I will: gather per-host traces, check kernel selection logs, and try a quick canary rollback of the catalog alias to verify.

Connor
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Embedding queries — p99 spike since catalog update

Quick technical readout from infra:
- The catalog rollout changed the default quantization profile; for some hosts that still have older driver/kernel combos we hit a slow path in the attention kernels. That increases per-token CPU and forces more frequent L2/VCache evictions (explains KV cache misses).
- Also noticed that the batching selector started grouping requests with longer seq_len when the variant changed; this increased average batch size and latency tail.

Mitigation plan (I can execute immediately with approval):
1) Roll the catalog alias for RapidRetail back to the previous non-quantized variant (can be scoped to their account).
2) Disable auto-rollout of quantized variants for the catalog until we have a kernel compatibility gate.
3) Increase short-term concurrency limits for their dedicated pool to reduce queuing while rollback propagates.

I'll stage the rollback in canary and run a small traffic test; will post traces (perf-traces-0316.zip).

Hannah
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, VP-Eng <vp_eng@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: alice@rapidretail.com
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: RapidRetail embedding latency — exec brief & proposed customer remediation

Team — escalating to leadership and VP Eng. RapidRetail is an active pilot (DEAL-8392) and is seeing production impact. Summary:
- Incident: embeddings p99 latency regression after catalog rollout that swapped to a quantized model variant (triggered 2026-03-15 ~02:10Z).
- Impact: timeouts in two pipelines; customer-reported.
- Proposed immediate actions: scoped rollback for RapidRetail, temporary service credits for impacted window, and a compatibility gate for catalog rollouts.

Requesting approval to proceed with the rollback and a small goodwill credit (equivalent to 10% of March hosted usage) to keep the account on track for the close. I will coordinate the customer comms once infra confirms rollback metrics.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, alice@rapidretail.com
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: RapidRetail embedding latency — rollback complete & remediation

Status update for the thread and for RapidRetail (cc'ed):
- Action taken: rolled the catalog alias back to "embed-small-v2" for RapidRetail at 15:12 PDT after canary verification.
- Observed outcome: p95 reduced from ~520ms to ~210ms; p99 reduced from ~1.2s to ~430ms within 18 minutes of rollback. Queuing reduced on their dedicated pool.
- Attachments: rollback_summary_0316.md (short timeline), perf-traces-0316.zip (before/after traces), postmortem-plan-0316.docx (next steps).

Next steps:
1) We will pause auto-promote of quantized variants and add a kernel compatibility check to the rollout pipeline.
2) Infra to run a rolling job to re-benchmark quantized variants across our node images and report back within 72 hours.
3) CS (Marissa) to send a short executive note and credit proposal to RapidRetail; Lauren to approve credits up to the amount discussed.

Alice — apologies for the impact. We will follow up with a formal postmortem and a remediation package.

Lauren
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
